FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 23 May 1989, after the draft 
finalized by the Shipbuilding Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering 
Division Council. 

The main aim of this standard is to give clear and unambiguous definitions for each term so as to be 
understood identically by all specialists concerned. 

A single standardized term is established for each item. The use of synonyms for the standardized 
terms shall not be permitted. 

For some of the standardized terms, words given in parentheses may be omitted, thereby allowing 
their short form to be used in cases where there is no risk of misinterpretation. 

In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from ISO 7255-1985 'Shipbuilding — 
Active control units of ships — Vocabulary', issued by the International Organization for Standardiza- 
tion ( ISO ). 



IS 12712 : 1989 



Indian Standard 



SHIPBUILDING — MEANS OF ACTIVE 
CONTROL OF SHIPS' MANOEUVRING - 
GLOSSARY OF TERMS 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard defines terms applicable to the 
means of active control of ships' manoeuvring. 

2 TERMINOLOGY 

2.1 Means of Active Control of Ships 

A device with an individual prime mover creating 
a thrust at some angle to the centreline plane of 
the vessel. 

2.2 ( Ship ) Thruster 

A means of active control of a ship having the 
working member in a tunnel located in the ship's 
hull ( or in a nozzle outside ) and creating a thrust 
at right angles to the centreline plane of the vessel. 

2.3 ( Ship ) Retractable Thruster 

Ship thruster whose lower part with the propeller 
in a nozzle can be lifted vertically inside the hull 
to an inoperable position. 

2.4 ( Ship ) Rudder-Propeller Unit 

A means of active control of a ship having the 
working member outside ( or inside ) the ship's 
hull and creating a thrust whose direction may be 
changed in respect to the centreline plane of the 
vessel. 

2.5 ( Ship ) Rotatable Rudder-Propeller 

A propelling and steering device with the propeller 
( or propeller in a nozzle ) creating a thrust whose 
direction can be changed within the range of 0° to 



360° when rotating the device relative to a vertical 
axis perpendicular to the propeller axis. 

2.6 ( Ship ) Swivelling Rotatable Rudder-Propeller 

A rotatable rudder-propeller whose lower part 
with the propeller ( or propeller in a nozzle ) can 
be hinged around a horizontal axis to an inoperable 
position. 

2.7 ( Ship ) Retractable Rotatable Rudder-Propeller 

A rotatable rudder-propeller whose lower part 
with the propeller ( or propeller in a nozzle ) can 
be lifted vertically inside the hull to an inoperable 
position. 

2.8 ( Ship ) Active Rudder 

A propelling and steering device having the 
working member in the rudder blade and creating 
a thrust whose direction can be changed within the 
rudder angle limits. 

2.9 ( Ship ) Vertical-Axis Propeller 

A propelling and steering device having a vertical 
axis propeller installed flush with the bottom of 
the vessel and creating a thrust whose direction 
can be changed from 0° to 360° starboard or port, 
by changing the angle of the vanes* 

2.10 ( Ship ) Rotatable Water Jet 

A propelling and steering device located inside the 
hull and creating a thrust whose direction may be 
changed ( smoothly or discretely ) within the range 
of 0° to 360° starboard or port when the rotatable 
device directing the water jet changes its position. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a weSl defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the 
producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BTS for conformity 
to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country.

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the 
course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade 
designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS.
